haiku-low.q1: No. Cursors never go to the document service or Postgres. They are written to Redis and published on the presence channel only.
haiku-low.q2: At most one cursor per 50 ms per client. The node enforces the same limit per connection and silently drops faster cursors, with no reply.
haiku-low.q3: It holds the cursor, replacing any older held cursor from that connection. It draws it once its appliedRev reaches that rev.
haiku-low.q4: It draws at transformPosition(pos, rev, appliedRev). If that throws HistoryGone (more than 500 revisions old), it drops the caret until the sender's next cursor.
haiku-low.q5: One avatar per userId, and one caret per user, from the most recently arrived cursor. The user leaves the list only when the last connId for that userId is removed.
haiku-low.q6: After a clean tab close, well under 2 s. After the gateway node dies, within about 40 s at most, under the 45 s requirement.
haiku-low.q7: In Redis, the primary, per connection: key pc:{docId}:{connId}, plus a per-document index set. Each live node rewrites its connections' entries every 10 s, with a 30 s expiry.
haiku-low.q8: Entries expire after 30 s without refresh. Within 10 s, the sweep on a surviving node removes their connIds from the index and publishes leave to other clients.
haiku-low.q9: Accepted cursors are published on presence:{docId}, and subscribed nodes deliver them to their sockets. Same-node delivery is NOT STATED beyond that channel.
haiku-low.q10: The node subscribes before reading the snapshot and buffers channel messages, sending them after the snapshot in order. Messages are idempotent upserts or deletes.
haiku-low.q11: The snapshot includes each entry's latest cursor {rev, pos, seq}, so an idle user's caret shows immediately.
haiku-low.q12: The receiver stores the last seq per connId and ignores any cursor whose seq is at or below the stored one.

sonnet.q1: No. Cursors never go to the document service or to Postgres. They go to Redis (the entry) and the presence channel.
sonnet.q2: At most one cursor per 50 ms per client, always sending the latest position last. The node enforces the same limit per connection and silently drops faster ones, with no reply.
sonnet.q3: It holds the cursor (replacing any older held one for that connection). Each time appliedRev moves, it re-checks held cursors and draws each one whose rev is now reached, at transformPosition.
sonnet.q4: It is drawn at transformPosition(pos, rev, appliedRev), and the drawn caret is moved forward the same way as more revisions are applied. If transformPosition throws HistoryGone (rev older than the 500 revisions kept), the caret is dropped and reappears at the sender's next cursor.
sonnet.q5: Each tab has its own connId but the same userId, so one avatar is shown. Only one caret is drawn per user (from the connection whose cursor arrived most recently). The user disappears when the last connId with that userId is removed.
sonnet.q6: After a clean tab close: well under 2 s. After node death: at most about 40 s (within the required 45 s).
sonnet.q7: In Redis (the primary is the source of truth), per connection: an entry pc:{docId}:{connId} (userId, name, colour, nodeId, latest cursor) with a 30 s TTL, plus an index set pd:{docId} (60 s TTL). Each node rewrites its open connections' entries every 10 s, which resets the expiry.
sonnet.q8: Nothing is done by the crashed node. Its entries expire within 30 s, then another node's sweep (every 10 s) finds connIds in the index with no entry, removes them with SREM, and the node whose SREM removed the id publishes leave on the channel. Other nodes pass it on to their clients.
sonnet.q9: The sender's node stores the cursor in memory, writes it to the Redis entry, and publishes it on presence:{docId}. Nodes subscribed to the channel (including the sender's own node) receive it and forward it to their clients. The sender gets no echo. NOT STATED whether the sender's own node's other local viewers get it by a separate local path; the document only describes the channel.
sonnet.q10: The node subscribes to the channel before it reads the index and entries. Channel messages arriving meanwhile are buffered and sent after the snapshot, in order. Messages are idempotent upserts or deletes keyed by connId, and the client replaces its map with the snapshot, then applies the later messages.
sonnet.q11: The snapshot includes every entry's latest cursor {rev, pos, seq}, so an idle user's caret shows at once. The client treats snapshot cursors like cursor messages. Also, each client sends its first cursor once the document is loaded, so others see its caret even if it never moves.
sonnet.q12: The receiver keeps the last seq per connId and ignores any cursor with seq at or below the stored one. seq is per connection and increases by 1 for each cursor.
